title: Spanish Colonial Revival
summary: Stucco walls and red tile roofs drawn from Spanish and Mexican architecture, popularized in California after the 1915 Panama-California Exposition.

title: Craftsman
summary: Handcrafted-looking homes with low-pitched roofs, wide eaves and exposed beams, tied to the Arts and Crafts movement.

title: Mid-Century Modern
summary: Postwar design with clean lines, large glass walls and an easy flow between indoors and outdoors.

title: Pueblo Revival
summary: Flat roofs, rounded corners and earth-toned stucco modeled on Pueblo and Spanish adobe building traditions.

title: Beaux-Arts
summary: Grand, symmetrical, classically ornamented public buildings influenced by the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris.

title: Art Deco
summary: Geometric ornament, a strong vertical emphasis and metallic accents, seen in the skyscrapers of the 1920s and 1930s.

title: Creole & Shotgun
summary: Two New Orleans house types: Creole cottages and townhouses from the French and Spanish colonial eras, and narrow shotgun houses with rooms in a row.

title: Chicago School
summary: Early steel-frame commercial buildings with large windows and little ornament, developed in Chicago after the 1871 fire.
